My father went to Catholic school and believed the "bible is the greatest book of fiction ever written". My mother believed so much as to tech her kids right from wrong (based on vague protestant standards), but never attended a church. She felt she didn't fit in with the other ladies. I had one aunt who was "super sister Christian" and every family event chase my atheist grandfather around the house trying to "lay hands on him" in prayer. So I grew up very "non-churched".

However, after my parents had a brutal divorce with lots of custody battles I was angry and hurt. Even worse, we were poor - destitute poor. My mother had ways to hide it, but if CPS had been called we would have been pulled. We asked for help from churches in the area and were shunned because my mom was "divorced" (aka undeserving poor). A few years later my mom got into a crummy relationship and ended up pregnant. She gave the babies up for adoption. This was in the late 80's/90's before the world had a social conscious. We lived in a small community and everyone talked. Rumors were my mom sold her babies (terrible right?). Because of this and being so poor I was BRUTALLY made fun of in school. I had no friends and would sit in the library durring lunch because I couldn't bear to sit by myself and eat in the caffateria alone. I would cry so hard at night because life sucked so bad.

For some reason, I can't tell you why Bible stories told to me as a kid started popping up in my head. Eventually I found a bible that had heavy commentary that I related too. I connected to the characters. By this time in highschool the people who were making me were far from Christian. Most would mock God. My disdain for those bastereds pushed me to study it more. I still hadn't accepted Jesus as my God. I could tell you lots of stuff, but I hadn't submitted my will to him yet. Then one day I was invited to attend a Billy Ghram conference. At that conference was the first time I truly felt God. I can't explain it other than an overwhelming experience of emotions stronger than you have ever felt in your life. When people say they hear from God, they do. It was like someone was speaking to my heart asking me over and over, "will you trust me?". After contemplating that question for 2 1/2 hours I finally stepped down onto the main floor and said the salvation prayer. The BEST part was when I felt down in the dumps in college a few years later. I was at Barns and Noble questioning my faith and half heartedly mocked, "where's my sign God?". A few minutes later I was looking through the Christian section and picked up the book, "A Case for Faith". In the intro the author was describing a Billy Ghram event that sounded just Ike my experience. At the very end the author reviels the location- it WAS my experience! Which is unusual because it was in Indiana. Not some big city that is talked about all the time like NY or LA. After I read that God asked, do you Still trust me?
